title: IQNN-CS: Interpretable Quantum Neural Network for Credit Scoring
abstract_summary: The paper introduces IQNN-CS, a hybrid classical–quantum framework that combines a variational quantum neural network with adapted post-hoc explanation methods for multiclass credit risk classification. It proposes a novel Inter-Class Attribution Alignment (ICAA) metric to quantify attribution divergence across predicted classes and evaluates the approach on two real-world credit datasets, demonstrating competitive performance and enhanced interpretability while highlighting dataset-dependent behavior.
methodology_description: The authors propose IQNN-CS, a hybrid classical–quantum pipeline for multiclass credit scoring. Raw tabular credit data are class-balanced (undersampling or SMOTE as appropriate), standardized, and reduced via PCA to a quantum-compatible dimensionality. A classical preprocessing block (fully connected layers with ReLU) maps PCA components to a latent vector which is angle-encoded onto NQ qubits (AngleEmbedding). A variational quantum circuit (multi-layer StronglyEntanglingLayers) parameterized by θ is applied; Pauli-Z expectation values per qubit are measured and concatenated into a classical postprocessing head with dropout and linear layers that output logits for C classes. The system is trained end-to-end using a class-weighted cross-entropy / negative log-likelihood loss, optimized with AdamW and a learning-rate scheduler; quantum gradients use the parameter-shift rule. Post-hoc interpretability combines gradient-based attributions (saliency, gradient×input, Integrated Gradients, SmoothGrad), occlusion sensitivity, prototype/example matching in the quantum activation space (cosine similarity), latent-space visualization (t-SNE), and a new Inter-Class Attribution Alignment (ICAA) metric that computes pairwise cosine similarities between class-specific attribution vectors to quantify attribution divergence across predicted classes. Model selection uses stratified train/validation/test splits with early stopping on validation loss. Evaluation reports standard classification metrics (accuracy, per-class precision/recall/F1, macro F1) plus interpretability artifacts (attribution maps, ICAA matrices, occlusion curves, and t-SNE embeddings).

Both are structured tabular credit-score datasets with categorical and numerical attributes and multiclass labels (Low / Average / High risk).

pipeline_steps: Preprocess and balance data; apply StandardScaler and PCA to reduce to d_PCA dimensions (6 components used in experiments).
Classical preprocessing: linear layer → ReLU → linear to produce latent vector matching quantum input size.
Encode latent features onto NQ qubits using AngleEmbedding (rotation gates per feature).
Apply variational quantum circuit: 4 layers of StronglyEntanglingLayers on 6 qubits; measure Pauli-Z expectation values for each qubit.
Concatenate measured expectations and feed to classical postprocessing head (dropout + linear) to produce logits over C classes.
Compute class-weighted cross-entropy / negative log-likelihood loss.

Optimize parameters end-to-end with AdamW (lr 0.01), learning-rate scheduler (StepLR or cosine annealing mentioned), 50 epochs, early stopping on validation loss; quantum gradients via parameter-shift (s = π/2).

Post-hoc interpretability: compute gradient-based attributions for each class (saliency, grad×input, Integrated Gradients, SmoothGrad), occlusion sensitivity curves by masking top features, example/prototype retrieval using cosine similarity on QNN activations, compute ICAA matrix as cosine similarities between per-class attribution vectors, and visualize latent quantum activations with t-SNE.

key_findings: [supported] IQNN-CS: a hybrid classical–quantum neural network architecture for multiclass credit scoring, implemented end-to-end with PennyLane/TorchLayer.

[supported] Introduced Inter-Class Attribution Alignment (ICAA), a metric that computes cosine similarity between class attribution vectors to quantify attribution divergence across predicted classes.

[supported] Proposed and evaluated a post-hoc interpretability pipeline that combines gradient-based attribution (saliency, gradient×input, integrated gradients, SmoothGrad), occlusion sensitivity, prototype matching in quantum activation space, and latent-space (t-SNE/PCA) visualizations.

[supported] Empirically evaluated IQNN-CS on two publicly available credit datasets using a 6-qubit variational quantum circuit (4 StronglyEntanglingLayers) with angle encoding simulated on default.qubit.
[supported] On Dataset 1 the model achieved the reported perfect performance: 100% accuracy and 100% macro F1-score.

[supported] On Dataset 2 the model achieved reported accuracy of 77.3% with class-wise metrics: Low class precision 0.64, recall 0.97, F1 0.77; Average class precision 0.73, recall 0.84, F1 0.78; High class precision 0.95, recall 0.67, F1 0.79.

[supported] Observed training dynamics: rapid, stable convergence with tightly clustered loss/accuracy curves on Dataset 1; noisy, less stable training and a large train-validation gap on Dataset 2 indicating poorer generalization.

[supported] Interpretability outcomes: Dataset 1 showed concentrated, stable feature attributions and well-separated quantum latent embeddings; Dataset 2 showed diffuse/noisy attributions and overlapping latent embeddings, correlating with lower classification performance.

[supported] Empirically found occlusion analysis and the proposed ICAA metric to be especially useful for detecting class-discriminative attribution structure and regions of model indecision in these experiments.

[supported] Prototype (example-based) matching in the quantum activation space found same-class nearest neighbors for Dataset 1 but mixed-class high-similarity influences for Dataset 2, signaling ambiguous internal representations.

[speculative] The authors argue that IQNN-CS (and similar interpretable QNN frameworks) provides a practical path toward transparent and accountable QML models suitable for deployment under financial regulation.
[speculative] General claims in the introduction that QNNs can encode/process high-dimensional structured data with fewer resources and represent complex decision boundaries for domains like finance.
[speculative] The broader assertion that interpretability-first QML frameworks will be essential as quantum computing technology matures.
results_summary: The paper introduces IQNN-CS, a hybrid classical–quantum neural network framework for multiclass credit scoring together with a post-hoc interpretability suite and a novel Inter-Class Attribution Alignment (ICAA) metric. Implemented with PennyLane and simulated on default.qubit, the model (6 qubits, 4 StronglyEntanglingLayers) was tested on two public credit datasets. On Dataset 1 the authors report perfect classification (100% accuracy/F1) with stable training and concentrated, class-discriminative attributions; on Dataset 2 the model attained 77.3% accuracy and exhibited noisy training, overlapping latent embeddings, and less reliable attributions. The interpretability analyses (occlusion, gradient methods, prototype matching, ICAA) are used to diagnose when the model’s internal logic is coherent (Dataset 1) versus ambiguous (Dataset 2). The authors emphasize that ICAA and occlusion were particularly informative for revealing class-wise reasoning and regions of indecision.
performance_claims: Dataset 2 class-wise metrics (reported): Low class precision 0.64, recall 0.97, F1 0.77; Average class precision 0.73, recall 0.84, F1 0.78; High class precision 0.95, recall 0.67, F1 0.79.
Model architecture: 6 qubits, 4 StronglyEntanglingLayers, angle encoding, PCA to 6 components (experimental configuration).
Training: 50 epochs, batch size 16, AdamW optimizer, learning rate 0.01 (experimental configuration).
quantum_advantage_detail: The paper does not claim or demonstrate a quantum computational advantage. Experiments run on a classical simulator (PennyLane default.qubit), no comparison versus classical baselines is provided, and the authors explicitly state the goal is interpretability rather than showing quantum supremacy or outperforming classical models.
limitations: The authors do not aim to demonstrate quantum supremacy or to outperform classical machine learning models; the work focuses on interpretability rather than superiority.
Interpretability for quantum machine learning is still nascent and lacks standardized tools; the paper adapts classical methods and introduces ICAA as a first step.

Model performance and interpretability strongly depend on dataset characteristics and alignment with the model's inductive bias — Dataset 2 showed unstable training, poorer generalization, and overlapping latent representations.

Gradient-based explanation methods were observed to be inconsistent and noisy for some predictions, especially on more complex/noisy data; the authors caution the use of these methods in quantum settings.
Attribution reliability and explanation clarity degrade on more complex datasets; example-based attributions sometimes align with incorrect classes despite high confidence.

key_ideas: #idea:hybrid-approach — Introduces IQNN-CS: an end-to-end hybrid classical–quantum pipeline for multiclass credit scoring combining PCA, a small classical encoder, angle-encoding onto qubits, a variational quantum circuit (StronglyEntanglingLayers) and a classical postprocessing head.

#idea:near-term-feasibility — Demonstrates a NISQ-scale implementation (6 qubits, 4 quantum layers) on a state-vector simulator, arguing practicality for small tabular credit datasets and emphasizing interpretability for deployment.

#idea:quantum-advantage — Authors report "competitive performance and enhanced interpretability" on two real-world Kaggle credit datasets using QNN-based model and introduce the Inter-Class Attribution Alignment (ICAA) metric to quantify attribution divergence between predicted classes.
#limitation:simulation-only — All experiments are run on PennyLane default.qubit (CPU simulator) with no experiments on real quantum hardware.
#limitation:no-empirical-validation — Claims of competitive performance are not supported by comparisons to classical baselines or other quantum models (no baseline models reported).
#limitation:data-encoding — Uses PCA to reduce to 6 components and angle-encoding; this preprocessing hides potential encoding costs and may limit applicability to higher-dimensional real-world data.
#limitation:qubit-count — Evaluation is restricted to 6 qubits and small circuit depth, leaving open questions about scalability to production-sized credit datasets.
#limitation:noise — Experiments use noise-free simulation (default.qubit) and do not assess impact of hardware noise or apply noise-aware/error-mitigation techniques.
contradictions: The paper asserts "competitive performance and enhanced interpretability" of the QNN approach but provides no classical or quantum baseline comparisons and runs only noise-free simulator experiments — this undermines the empirical support for any claimed quantum advantage or superiority over classical methods.
